title: AI Trading BOT
author: Elfwood86
selftext:
My AI Bot decided to buy:

HCA: 0.233525 shares

IT: 0.5343572 shares

KR: 1.6631183 shares

Paper Trades. My BOT is allowed to hold 5bstocks at a time. It decided to buy 3 stocks today.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
sizes like 0.2335 look like it's sizing by dollar amount per name, which is the sane way to do it with 5 slots. I'd save the reason it gave for each buy next to the fill. in a month the useful question is whether the reasons that lost look different from the ones that won.

if you'd rather not build the grading side yourself, Quantradin grades exactly this kind of paper record, I built it, no look-ahead, never touches real money. quantradin.com.

replies.author: Elfwood86
replies.body: It is limiting how much it can invest per stock per day. This is based on the script not AI. AI does pick the stocks.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: good, that's the right split. with the cap in the script, a confident pick still can't size itself up. does it cap total exposure across all five too, or only per name?

comments.author: Sharp_Syrup_7052
comments.body: Did it say why those three specifically - and did you document it?

replies.author: Elfwood86
replies.body:
It didnt say why those three automatically. So, I had to ask it and this is the response for Gartner:


IT — Gartner: Probably the most interesting quality/business-model selection. Gartner's Q2 adjusted EPS increased 23.8%, net income increased 14.4%, free cash flow increased 8.9%, and it repurchased $547 million of stock. The weakness is growth: reported revenue actually declined 0.6%, while FX-neutral contract value grew only 1.7% year over year. � So your bot appears to be buying strong profitability/cash generation despite relatively sluggish top-line growth.

replies.author: Elfwood86
replies.body: HCI — HCI Group: This is the most aggressive of the three. Q2 was strong: net income rose to $83 million from $70 million a year earlier, diluted EPS increased to $5.60, and gross premiums earned increased 6%. Lower reinsurance costs also helped. � The major concern is catastrophe exposure—HCI is heavily exposed to property insurance, particularly Florida, so hurricanes and other severe weather can create substantial volatility. The stock had also fallen from roughly $188 in mid-September to about $175 by Sept. 28, which may have helped it pass your bot's valuation/technical screens.
